header.stance: 油價推升通膨補償，回購漲幅部分回吐

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 油價推升通膨補償，美債回吐部分漲幅

油價上漲帶動通膨補償攀升，美債週四回吐部分由回購消息帶動的漲幅。5年、10年與30年期殖利率各上升4個基點，分別收在4.39%、4.69%與5.23%，2年期則維持4.19%。財政部長貝森特表示，回購可能超過原訂規模，也承諾加強財政整頓，但尚未提出降低借款需求的具體措施。

30年期殖利率盤中一度升至5.27%，貝森特談話後賣壓減輕，收盤回升幅度為前一天9個基點降幅中的4個基點，並非全數回吐。10年期實質殖利率持平於2.35%，損益兩平通膨率則上升4個基點至2.34%。川普威脅對伊朗及其貿易夥伴採取行動，布蘭特原油上漲1.77%至$93.24。財政部吸收更多長債的承諾仍在，通膨前景卻轉趨不利。

AI融資又增加了一項潛在供給。Broadcom正討論透過特殊目的架構，結合優先擔保債與次順位債，最多借入$1,000億，為Anthropic等客戶的晶片及基礎設施籌資。交易仍在協商，但規模已讓市場重新注意整體建置需要多少資本。一般公司債發行仍獲得訂單支持，Vylor與Thales最終定價都明顯低於初步利差指引。

## 貝森特承諾擴大支持，市場等待財政細節

貝森特表示，9月9日起的回購可能超過目前每檔$40億的規劃，並強調政府有更廣泛的工具維持市場秩序。川普已指派他與預算主管Russ Vought推動財政整頓，預計本週底或下週初公布。貝森特認為，關稅收入、經濟成長與減少詐欺可改善財政，赤字也很可能已見頂；但談話未附帶具體支出、收入或債務管理措施。

融資需求的規模仍是主要難題。宣布加倍前，9月9日至11月4日的暫定時程僅安排最多$140億長債回購。JPMorgan估計，未來幾個會計年度的資金缺口超過$3.5兆，即使經濟接近充分就業，赤字仍約占GDP的6%，公共債務已突破$40兆。額外回購可改變投資人持有的到期結構，資金也可能來自更頻繁的國庫券發行；但若要持續減少借款，仍得改變政府實際收支。

投資人也質疑，為何季度策略公布僅兩週就意外調整。JPMorgan、Jefferies策略師及PGIM投資人警告，發債流程若變得難以預測，可能提高長債需要支付的溢價。PGIM共同投資長、財政部借款諮詢委員會成員Greg Peters估計，公告讓政府在週三$160億20年期標售上節省約$2億成本，但該次需求仍平淡。單次標售成本降低，不代表市場對未來融資指引的疑慮已經消除。

價格下跌時，交易仍活躍。按原始面額計算，美債成交額為$1.246兆，較週三放量後的水準減少9.0%；一般附息公債為$1.016兆，減少8.6%。20年以上債券成交$1,379億，共50,919筆，交易商與客戶之間的交易占面額47.2%，該天期成交額較前日減少19.2%。市場仍有持續的雙向交易，並非交投突然萎縮。

殖利率曲線轉陡，2年與10年期利差擴大4個基點至50個基點，2年與30年期擴大4個基點至104個基點。30年期殖利率仍較1個月前高12個基點。20年以上政府債指數下跌0.81%，長天期高評等公司債指數約跌0.85%至0.90%。LQD下跌0.48%，HYG與JNK則約跌0.19%至0.20%，損失較集中在長久期投資組合。

Citi將3個月美元指數預測由102.12下修至98.34，並將歐元兌美元預測上調至1.1750，理由包括美國殖利率下降，以及回購引發的金融壓抑疑慮。但這是展望，並非週四即時走勢：美元指數在週三大跌後，當日近乎持平於98.796，油價、美債殖利率反彈及AI相關資金流入均提供支撐。黃金期貨仍上漲2.07%至$4,582.30。

這樣的政策組合也留下一個Fed必須面對的問題。Warsh鼓勵投資人依經濟數據自行定價，財政部卻認為長債殖利率未反映基本面。若擴大回購顯著降低房貸與企業融資成本，可能在通膨仍高於目標時放鬆金融情勢；若效果主要限於改善舊券流動性，對貨幣緊縮程度的影響就會較小。

## Daly主張耐心，Musalem仍擔心通膨降不下來

川普預告週一記者會將公布對伊朗的經濟施壓細節，包括與德黑蘭往來的國家、銀行及企業。中國是伊朗原油最大買家。收盤時措施尚未明朗，但若執法轉強，可能影響波斯灣運輸受阻期間，仍讓石油持續流動的管道及安排。

布蘭特當日上漲後，近1週漲幅達7.09%；WTI漲幅較小，為0.51%，收在$86.27。10年期損益兩平通膨率近1週上升10個基點，當日增加的4個基點更占名目殖利率升幅的全部，與週三實質殖利率下降帶動行情形成對比。TIPS成交額增加25.7%至$367億，交易商與客戶間交易占65.9%。這是交易活動而非通膨避險淨買入，但通膨補償上升之際，抗通膨債的換手確實更熱絡。

舊金山Fed總裁Mary Daly認為，沒有急於預防性升息的理由。她判斷關稅、油價與AI帶來的價格衝擊可能是暫時的，勞動市場並未助長通膨，近期資料也未顯示廣泛的持續性壓力。就業偏弱、核心通膨溫和與零售銷售下滑後，市場反映九月升息機率約30%，低於七月底逾70%。

聖路易斯Fed總裁Alberto Musalem則較不願等待。他表示原本會支持七月升息，並認為若不加強緊縮，未來18個月通膨無法回到2%的風險較大。他與Daly今年都沒有投票權。不過，Musalem仍認為通膨預期受到控制，長債殖利率偏高主要來自政府融資及AI資本需求，而不是Fed公信力下降。他對通膨的擔憂，與對長債賣壓成因的判斷，是兩件不同的事。

七月會議紀錄也顯示，AI讓政策判斷更複雜。部分官員目前只看到零星消費價格影響，其他人卻認為投資熱潮已經、或即將推升總需求。有些工作遭到取代，資料中心周邊卻缺乏電工、水管工及營建人力。官員也討論非銀行與區域銀行增加的信用曝險：若AI前景不如預期，股價下跌可能拖累消費並使貸款人承壓，而預期中的生產力效益尚未到來。

週四股市同樣反映經濟分歧。S&P 500下跌0.87%，Nasdaq 100跌0.72%、連續第5日走低，VIX上升7.52%至16.01。Walmart銷售令人失望，股價創2022年以來最大跌幅，拖累大盤；半導體指數卻在前1週跌逾5%後反彈0.53%。面向消費者的企業轉弱，科技投資仍持續，傳遞給決策官員的訊號並不一致。

## Broadcom洽談最高$1,000億融資，一般新債仍有買盤

貸款人正討論為Broadcom特殊目的融資提供$600億至$700億優先擔保債，由公司保證其中一部分，另可能加入$300億次順位債。借款總額最高可達$1,000億，資金可能分批投入，Blackstone與Apollo也在洽談參與。這些金額都尚未成為已完成發行。

該計畫延續先前$350億的AI XPV交易：Broadcom為大部分債務提供支持，Apollo、Blackstone等投資人為租予Anthropic的客製晶片出資，讓優先債取得投資級評等並降低成本。若新架構規模大幅提高，又加入次順位債，投資人就得逐一評估保證、設備價值與租約現金流，不能將所有債權都視為一般Broadcom公司債。

合作計畫目標是支應逾20GW運算容量，約相當於20座核電廠的輸出，總需求將達數千億美元。因此資金投入順序十分重要：多少進入公開債市、多少留在銀行或私募資本機構帳上，以及提用速度多快。分階段建置可將融資需求分散到不同時間，而非一次把全數供給帶進市場。

Vylor則已在自Corteva分拆前，完成$11億5年期及10年期債券。10年期利差由初步約135個基點，收窄至美債之上100個基點。資金將用於向Corteva另一子公司EIDP支付分配款，另有$14.2億EIDP債券已提出交換為Vylor債務。定價需求良好，同時也將槓桿及對母公司的支付移入即將獨立的種子業務。

Thales發行€10億，支應以€39億收購海事機器人公司Exail。4年與8年期各半，合計訂單超過€25.5億，最終分別定在mid-swap之上45與65個基點，均較初步指引收窄32.5個基點，預期評等為A−。荷姆茲海峽水雷危機提高了水下無人載具需求，也支撐這筆融資背後的策略擴張。

其他信用資產的利差緩衝也偏薄。美國大型高評等企業利差約80個基點，接近30年低點；在這個水準，擴大約12個基點，就可能抵銷1年的額外收益。絕對殖利率仍吸引買盤，但對利差損失的保護已減少。

銀行資本債的對比更明顯。全球AT1殖利率約5.7%，高於投資級公司債的不到5%及政府債的約3.7%；其滾動10日波動率卻據報比高評等公司債低75%。CoCo利差首次跌破200個基點，BNP Paribas也以該行美元AT1歷來最低重設利差發債。票息收入與資金流入支撐價格，並不代表取消配息、不贖回或優先吸收損失的風險已經消失。

## 保險業調查延伸至評等機構，片廠貸款人保留部分債權

聯邦調查人員要求Egan-Jones提供替Delaware Life與Clear Spring評等的相關紀錄，兩家保險公司均由Mark Walter控制。Egan-Jones表示，本身並非調查對象或目標。兩家保險公司在二月收到傳票並進行內部檢視後，於六月揭露，逾$200億貸款因與Walter或其企業有關，原應歸類為關係人交易。

對單一評等機構的依賴規模，使這項調查具有財務意義。截至2025年底，Delaware Life的$320億債券投資組合中，約16%唯一已知的評等來自Egan-Jones；Clear Spring的$63億部位，占比至少50%。兩家公司自2024年以來已支付該機構$800萬。投資級評等可降低法定資本要求，因此相關紀錄可能涉及關係人曝險如何評估、背後配置多少資本。但調查本身尚不能證明評等機構違法，或債券已發生損失。

MBS Group的更新報導釐清了一項重整條款。據知情人士表示，貸款人將最多$9億債務轉為股權，同時取得$1億重整後債務，並同意再投入$4,000萬。這$1億是債權，而非股權估值。HPS與Oaktree如今取代Hackman Capital Partners及Affinius Capital，控制這家服務逾600個影視製作場地的公司。

同一批片廠投資也顯示再融資壓力。Hackman與Affinius於2019年以$6.5億向Carlyle買下MBS及Manhattan Beach Studios；Radford Studio後來因再融資失敗遭Goldman Sachs接管，Netflix正洽談以遠低於2021年$18.5億買價的金額收購。Deutsche Bank則在出售Television City的$3.375億債權，以及Manhattan Beach Studio的$2.4億票據。拍攝減少、2023年罷工與借款成本上升，使貸款人從收取利息，轉向出售債權或接管資產。

肯亞銀行面對疲弱民間信用，則增加持有政府證券。這類部位在2025年成長19%，占資產30%；放款僅成長6.6%，占KSh8.35兆資產負債表的48%。不良貸款率仍接近15%，為東非最高，政府積欠款項也壓迫借款人。即使主權債殖利率下降，仍不足以促使銀行大幅重返民間放款。

## 印度因會議紀錄下跌，澳洲就業與日本標售支撐債市

交易員重新解讀印度央行8月3日至5日會議紀錄後，殖利率明顯上升。10年期一度上升5個基點至6.87%，5年期一度升8個基點至6.53%。一致維持5.25%利率與中性立場，原先看來較偏鴿，紀錄中的討論卻不同：Poonam Gupta提到今年可能升息，Sanjay Malhotra警告價格壓力擴散，外部委員Ram Singh與Saugata Bhattacharya也提及重新調整或迅速行動。

先前支撐外匯存底與盧比流動性的外幣存款優惠又提前結束，增添重估壓力。Citi將預測的升息起點提前至十二月，預估累計50個基點，並認為若證據擴大，十月也可能行動。Goldman Sachs預期十二月與二月各升25個基點。這些仍是預測；已發生的是，投資人將先前因聲明偏溫和而建立的債券部位反向調整。

澳洲最新就業數據則偏弱。七月失業率升至4.5%，高於4.4%的市場預期，為近5年最高；就業人數減少15,800人，全數來自兼職，原先預期則增加12,000人。澳幣一度下跌0.3%，3年期殖利率最多下降4個基點，十二月前升息機率由68%降至62%。RBA維持4.35%後，總裁Michele Bullock曾表示很可能還要再升息，央行也仍認為勞動市場略緊於充分就業水準。

今年較早的3次升息及稅制調整，已使房市轉弱。全國住宅價格比三月高點低2.8%，主要銀行房貸申請自五月中旬減少約10%至15%；六月當季新增投資型房貸下降逾10%，新南威爾斯州更降逾14%。政府在發行A$170億後，總債務短暫超過A$1兆，隨後到期償還預計會使其回到門檻以下。當週標售需求接近發行量5倍，AAA評等穩定，債務相對已開發國家仍低。

瑞典維持1.75%利率，已延續12個月，符合受訪19名經濟學家的共同預期。央行仍保留2026年稍晚升息的可能，條件是夏季通膨持續；目前核心通膨明顯低於2%，勞動市場也弱於預期。埃及則連續第4次維持存款與放款利率於19%及20%。七月物價雖未較前月上升，年通膨率卻加速至14.9%。戰事帶來的匯率及燃料進口風險，使降息暫停；外部融資則包括IMF約$18億及歐盟執委會€15億。

日本20年期標售需求尚可，但不算強勁。投標倍數略高於1年平均、低於前次，最大幾家國內交易商的需求分布均衡；尾差較七月擴大，最低得標價也不及標售前估計。不過，美國回購消息仍提供支撐，20年期殖利率下跌8個基點至3.695%，40年期下跌10個基點至4.05%。

另外的資金流資料顯示，外資賣壓集中在較敏感於政策的天期。七月海外投資人淨賣出¥1.28兆2年與5年期日本公債，為2006年7月以來最大流出，卻淨買入¥8,898億原始到期年限超過10年的債券。政府殖利率上升也傳至機構借款人：日本學生支援機構發行¥300億，票息1.689%，為2004年開始發債以來最高，較日本公債高1個基點。住宅金融支援機構¥103億住宅抵押貸款證券的票息創3.45%紀錄，部分房貸利率九月可能因此上調。

美股收盤後公布的日本七月扣除生鮮食品CPI年增1.8%，符合預期，較前月1.6%加速；整體CPI及扣除生鮮食品與能源的指標均增1.9%，能源價格在六月略降後上升0.6%。亞洲交易開始之際，這些資料與日圓疲弱、政府傾向九月或十月行動，共同增加近期升息的理由。

歐洲方面，面對2027年選舉，投資人已愈來愈能接受義大利殖利率低於法國。Meloni政府被視為較穩定且願意縮減赤字，法國則面臨艱難的預算協商。持有人結構也不同：義大利主權債僅9%由歐元區以外投資人持有，法國為26%；義大利家庭則持有14%。即使同受全球利率壓力，政治不確定性傳至兩國債市的程度仍可能不同。

## 接下來看財政措施、伊朗制裁執行與Broadcom融資條款

貝森特預告的措施，需要把成長、關稅與減少詐欺的論點，轉為可衡量的赤字及現金借款變化。具體方案可讓擴大回購獲得財政面的配合；否則，政府仍只是在龐大資金缺口下調整到期結構。

週一伊朗政策的影響，則取決於執法及實際油流。若限制出口、中國採購、運輸或保險，通膨補償可能持續上升；若執法有限，或替代管道仍暢通，壓力就會減輕。2年期殖利率目前仍維持4.19%，油價帶動的損益兩平通膨率變化，尚未轉為立即的Fed利率重估。

Broadcom接下來值得關注的是優先與次順位最終規模、保證範圍、擔保品及租約條件、評等與資金投入順序。銀行及私募資本機構留存多少部位，也有助判斷風險最終由誰承擔。最高融資金額呈現的是計畫企圖，實際籌資結果才會確立成本。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Oil takes back part of the Treasury rally

Treasuries gave back part of Wednesday's buyback-driven gains as higher oil prices lifted inflation compensation. Five-, 10- and 30-year yields each rose 4 basis points on Thursday, closing at 4.39%, 4.69% and 5.23%. The 2-year stayed at 4.19%. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said purchases could be larger than planned and promised a new focus on fiscal consolidation, but offered no detailed measures to reduce borrowing.

The 30-year yield had climbed to 5.27% intraday before Bessent's comments helped limit the selloff. Its closing increase reversed 4 of the previous day's 9-basis-point decline, not the whole rally. At 10 years, the real yield held at 2.35% while the breakeven rose 4 basis points to 2.34%. Brent gained 1.77% to $93.24 as President Donald Trump threatened action against Iran and its trading partners. Treasury's promise to absorb more long bonds remained in place; the inflation outlook had become less comfortable.

AI financing added another prospective source of supply. Broadcom was discussing a special-purpose structure that could borrow as much as $100 billion, combining senior secured and junior debt to fund chips and infrastructure for Anthropic and other users. The deal was still being negotiated, but its scale brought fresh attention to how much capital the build-out could require. Conventional corporate deals continued to attract orders, with Vylor and Thales both pricing well inside initial indications.

## Bessent promises more support, while investors wait for fiscal detail

Buybacks due to start September 9 could exceed the currently planned $4 billion per issue, Bessent said, describing a broader toolkit for maintaining orderly markets. He also said Trump had assigned him and Budget Director Russ Vought to fiscal consolidation, with an announcement expected at the end of the week or early the next. Tariff revenue, growth and fraud reduction could improve the outlook, he argued, adding that there was a good chance the deficit had peaked. No accompanying spending, revenue or debt-management measures were specified.

The scale of the financing need remains the obstacle. The tentative September 9–November 4 calendar had allowed up to $14 billion of long-sector purchases before the announced doubling. JPMorgan estimates a funding gap above $3.5 trillion in coming fiscal years, with the deficit near 6% of GDP despite an economy close to full employment. Public debt has passed $40 trillion. Additional purchases can change which maturities investors hold, potentially funded by more frequent bill issuance, but a lasting reduction in borrowing requires a change in fiscal cash flows.

Investors also questioned the surprise revision just two weeks after Treasury published its quarterly strategy. JPMorgan and Jefferies strategists, along with PGIM investors, warned that a less predictable process could raise the premium demanded on long bonds. PGIM co-CIO Greg Peters, a Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee member, estimated that the announcement saved the government roughly $200 million on Wednesday's $16 billion 20-year auction. Demand at that sale was nevertheless tepid. A lower cost on one auction does not necessarily settle concerns about future financing guidance.

Trading remained active as prices retreated. Treasury turnover totaled $1.246 trillion in original-face par value, down 9.0% from Wednesday's surge. Nominal coupons accounted for $1.016 trillion, down 8.6%. Securities beyond 20 years traded $137.9 billion across 50,919 transactions, with dealer-to-customer activity representing 47.2% of par value; turnover in that bucket fell 19.2%. The data show continued two-way activity rather than a collapse in trading.

The curve steepened, with 2s10s widening 4 basis points to 50 and 2s30s widening 4 to 104. The long yield remained 12 basis points higher over a month. The 20-plus-year government bond index lost 0.81%, and long high-grade corporate indices fell about 0.85%–0.90%. LQD declined 0.48%, compared with roughly 0.19%–0.20% losses in HYG and JNK, putting the larger burden on long-duration portfolios.

Citi cut its three-month dollar-index forecast to 98.34 from 102.12 and raised its EUR/USD forecast to 1.1750. The bank cited lower US yields and concern about financial repression as channels through which buybacks could weaken the currency. That forecast did not describe Thursday's trading: the dollar index was nearly flat at 98.796 after Wednesday's sharp fall, while oil, higher Treasury yields and AI-related capital inflows provided support. Gold futures still gained 2.07% to $4,582.30.

The policy mix leaves an unresolved question for the Fed. Warsh has encouraged investors to follow economic data and form their own prices, while Treasury argues that long yields do not reflect fundamentals. If larger purchases materially lower mortgage and corporate borrowing costs, they could ease conditions while inflation remains above target. If they do little beyond improving liquidity in older bonds, their influence on monetary restraint will be smaller.

## Daly favors patience; Musalem remains concerned about inflation

Trump promised details of an economic campaign against Iran at a Monday press conference, including pressure on countries, banks and businesses that trade with Tehran. China is the dominant buyer of Iranian oil. Measures had not been specified by the close, but stronger enforcement could affect the routes and arrangements that have kept oil moving despite Gulf disruption.

Brent's increase took its weekly gain to 7.09%; WTI rose a smaller 0.51% to $86.27. Ten-year breakevens were 10 basis points higher over the week. Their 4-basis-point daily increase accounted for the entire rise in the nominal 10-year yield, in contrast to Wednesday's decline through real yields. TIPS turnover rose 25.7% to $36.7 billion, with dealer-to-customer trades representing 65.9%. That measures activity rather than net inflation buying, but inflation-linked securities were trading more heavily as compensation rose.

San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly saw no urgent case for a preemptive hike. She considered tariff, oil and AI price shocks likely to be temporary, found no labor-market contribution to inflation and saw no new evidence of broad persistence in recent releases. Markets priced about a 30% chance of a September increase, down from more than 70% at end-July, after weaker employment, subdued core inflation and falling retail sales.

St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem took a less patient position. He would have supported a July hike and saw a greater risk that inflation would fail to return to 2% over the next 18 months without tighter policy. Both he and Daly are nonvoters this year. Musalem nevertheless said expectations remained anchored and attributed high long yields to government financing and AI capital demand, not lost Fed credibility. His inflation concern and his explanation of the bond selloff were separate judgments.

The July minutes show why AI complicates that assessment. Some participants saw only selected consumer-price effects so far, while others thought the investment boom was already lifting aggregate demand or soon would. Job displacement in some businesses coexists with regional shortages of electricians, plumbers and construction workers around data centers. Officials also discussed growing nonbank and regional-bank credit exposure: disappointed AI expectations could lower equities, weaken consumption and put lenders under pressure before the hoped-for productivity gains arrive.

Thursday's equity performance reflected an uneven economy. The S&P 500 fell 0.87%, Nasdaq 100 lost 0.72% for a fifth decline, and VIX rose 7.52% to 16.01. Walmart's disappointing sales contributed to the broad decline, with its shares suffering their largest fall since 2022. Semiconductors, however, gained 0.53% after losing more than 5% over the preceding week. Weak consumer-facing businesses and continuing technology investment are giving policymakers different signals.

## Broadcom discusses up to $100 billion; ordinary new issues still find buyers

Lenders were discussing $60 billion–$70 billion of senior secured debt for Broadcom's special-purpose financing, with the company guaranteeing part of it, plus a possible $30 billion junior tranche. Borrowing could reach $100 billion and capital might be deployed incrementally. Blackstone and Apollo were in talks to participate. None of those amounts represented completed issuance.

The proposal builds on a $35 billion AI XPV transaction in which Broadcom backstopped most of the debt and Apollo, Blackstone and others financed custom chips leased to Anthropic. Sponsor support enabled senior tranches to obtain investment-grade ratings and lower costs. A much larger structure with junior debt would leave investors assessing the guarantee, equipment value and lease cash flows, rather than treating every claim as a conventional Broadcom obligation.

The partnership aims to fund more than 20 gigawatts of computing power—roughly the output of 20 nuclear plants—and will require hundreds of billions of dollars. Its scale makes the funding sequence important: how much enters public bond markets, how much stays with banks or private-capital firms, and how quickly the money is drawn. An incremental rollout would spread that demand over time rather than bring the full amount to market at once.

Vylor completed $1.1 billion of five- and 10-year bonds ahead of its separation from Corteva. The 10-year priced at 100 basis points over Treasuries, down from initial discussion near 135. Proceeds will fund a distribution to Corteva unit EIDP, while $1.42 billion of EIDP notes had been tendered for exchange into Vylor debt. Strong pricing accompanied a transfer of leverage and a parent payout into the soon-to-be independent seed business.

Thales raised €1 billion toward its €3.9 billion acquisition of maritime robotics company Exail. The equally sized four- and eight-year tranches drew more than €2.55 billion of orders and priced at 45 and 65 basis points over mid-swaps, each 32.5 basis points inside initial indications. The debt was expected to carry an A− rating. Demand for submarine drones has risen amid the Strait of Hormuz mine crisis, supporting the strategic expansion behind the financing.

Investors were accepting limited spread protection elsewhere. US blue-chip corporate spreads near 80 basis points were close to a three-decade low; widening of roughly 12 basis points would erase a year of incremental income at that level. Absolute yields continued to attract buyers even as the cushion against spread losses narrowed.

Bank capital presented a particularly striking comparison. Global additional Tier 1 debt yielded about 5.7%, versus less than 5% for IG corporates and about 3.7% for government bonds. Its rolling 10-day volatility was reported at 75% below high-grade corporate debt. CoCo spreads fell below 200 basis points for the first time, and BNP Paribas sold a dollar AT1 at its tightest reset spread in that currency. Coupon income and inflows supported prices, but neither removes coupon-cancellation, uncertain-call or first-loss risks.

## Insurer scrutiny reaches the rater; studio lenders retain debt as well as equity

Federal investigators sought Egan-Jones records concerning its work for Delaware Life and Clear Spring, two Mark Walter-controlled insurers. Egan-Jones said it was not a subject or target of the investigation. The insurers disclosed in June, after a February subpoena and internal review, that more than $20 billion of loans should have been classified as affiliated transactions because of connections to Walter or his businesses.

The size of their reliance on the rater gives the inquiry financial significance. At end-2025, Egan-Jones was the sole known rating provider for about 16% of Delaware Life's $32 billion bond portfolio and at least 50% of Clear Spring's $6.3 billion book. The insurers have paid it $8 million since 2024. Investment-grade ratings can reduce required regulatory capital, so the records could bear on how related-party exposures were assessed and supported by capital. The inquiry does not establish misconduct by the rater or losses on the bonds.

Updated reporting on MBS Group clarified a restructuring term: lenders received $100 million of take-back debt alongside the conversion of as much as $900 million of debt into equity, and agreed to invest another $40 million, according to people familiar with the deal. The $100 million is a debt claim, not an equity valuation. HPS and Oaktree now control a production-services company serving more than 600 entertainment locations, replacing Hackman Capital Partners and Affinius Capital.

The broader studio portfolio shows the refinancing strain. Hackman and Affinius paid Carlyle $650 million for MBS and Manhattan Beach Studios in 2019. Goldman Sachs later seized Radford Studio after refinancing failed; Netflix has discussed buying it for a fraction of the $1.85 billion paid in 2021. Deutsche Bank is marketing $337.5 million of Television City debt and a $240 million note on Manhattan Beach Studio. Slower filming, the 2023 strikes and higher borrowing costs have pushed lenders from collecting interest toward selling claims or taking control of assets.

Kenyan banks have responded to weak private credit by holding more government securities. Those holdings rose 19% in 2025 to 30% of assets, while loans and advances grew 6.6% and accounted for 48% of a KSh8.35 trillion balance sheet. Nonperforming loans remained near 15%, the highest ratio in East Africa, with state arrears pressuring borrowers. Lower sovereign yields have not been enough to draw banks back into more private lending.

## India sells off on minutes; Australian jobs and Japan's auction support bonds

Indian yields rose sharply as traders reassessed minutes from the August 3–5 RBI meeting. The 10-year climbed as much as 5 basis points to 6.87% and the 5-year as much as 8 to 6.53%. The unanimous hold at 5.25% and neutral stance had looked more dovish than the discussion that followed: Poonam Gupta raised the possibility of a hike this year, Sanjay Malhotra warned about broader price pressure, and external members Ram Singh and Saugata Bhattacharya mentioned recalibration or swift adjustment.

The reassessment followed the early closure of a foreign-currency deposit incentive that had supported reserves and rupee liquidity. Citi brought forward its forecast for tightening to December, expecting 50 basis points in total and describing October as possible if evidence broadened. Goldman Sachs expected 25-basis-point increases in December and February. These remain forecasts; the realized change was the reversal of positions accumulated after the initially reassuring statement.

Australia's fresh labor data pointed the other way. July unemployment rose to 4.5%, above the 4.4% consensus and the highest in nearly five years. Employment fell 15,800, entirely in part-time jobs, rather than rising by the expected 12,000. The Australian dollar fell as much as 0.3% and 3-year yields as much as 4 basis points. Pricing for a hike by December declined to 62% from 68%. Governor Michele Bullock had said another increase was quite possible after the RBA held at 4.35%, and the bank still viewed labor conditions as somewhat tighter than full employment.

Housing was already weakening after three earlier RBA increases and tax changes. National dwelling prices stood 2.8% below their March peak; mortgage applications at major banks fell roughly 10%–15% from mid-May, and new investor loans dropped more than 10% in the June quarter, including over 14% in New South Wales. Gross national debt temporarily exceeded A$1 trillion after A$17 billion of issuance, with maturities set to bring it back below that level. Demand at the week's sale was nearly five times the amount offered, AAA ratings remained stable, and debt was still low relative to developed-market peers.

Sweden held rates at 1.75% for a twelfth month, as all 19 surveyed economists expected. The Riksbank kept open the possibility of a later-2026 hike if summer inflation persisted, although core inflation remained clearly below 2% and labor conditions were weaker than expected. Egypt also held, keeping deposit and lending rates at 19% and 20% for a fourth meeting. July annual inflation accelerated to 14.9% despite no monthly increase. War-related currency and fuel-import risks have interrupted easing, while external financing included about $1.8 billion from the IMF and €1.5 billion from the European Commission.

Japan's 20-year auction attracted adequate, rather than emphatic, demand. Coverage was marginally above its one-year average but below the prior sale, with demand spread evenly among the largest domestic dealers. The tail widened from July and the lowest accepted price missed pre-sale estimates. Twenty-year yields nevertheless fell 8 basis points to 3.695%, and 40-year yields dropped 10 to 4.05%, helped by the US buyback announcement.

Separate flows showed foreign selling concentrated nearer the policy-sensitive end. Overseas investors sold a net ¥1.28 trillion of 2- and 5-year JGBs in July, the largest outflow since July 2006, while buying ¥889.8 billion of bonds originally issued with maturities beyond 10 years. Higher government yields were also reaching agency borrowers: Japan Student Services Organization sold ¥30 billion at a 1.689% coupon, its highest since issuance began in 2004 and 1 basis point over JGBs. Japan Housing Finance Agency set a record 3.45% coupon on ¥10.3 billion of residential mortgage-backed securities, raising the prospect of higher mortgage rates in September.

Released after the US close, Japanese July CPI excluding fresh food rose 1.8% from a year earlier, matching consensus and accelerating from 1.6%. Overall CPI and the measure excluding fresh food and energy both rose 1.9%; energy gained 0.6% after a slight June decline. The figures added to the case for a near-term BOJ hike as Asian trading began, alongside yen weakness and the government's preference for September or October action.

In Europe, investors have increasingly accepted lower Italian yields than French yields ahead of the 2027 elections. Meloni's government is viewed as more stable and committed to deficit reduction, while France faces difficult budget negotiations. Ownership also differs: only 9% of Italian sovereign debt is held outside the euro area, against 26% for France, and Italian households hold 14%. Those differences can alter each market's sensitivity to political uncertainty even under the same global rate pressure.

## Fiscal measures, Iran enforcement and the terms of Broadcom's financing

Bessent's promised announcement needs to translate growth, tariff and fraud-reduction arguments into measurable effects on deficits and cash borrowing. Detailed measures would give expanded buybacks a fiscal counterpart; without them, the government would still be adjusting maturities against a large funding gap.

Monday's Iran announcement will matter through enforcement and actual oil flows. Restrictions that constrain exports, Chinese purchases, shipping or insurance could prolong the rise in inflation compensation. Limited enforcement or continued alternative flows would soften that pressure. The 2-year yield has so far stayed at 4.19%, leaving a distinction between the oil-driven breakeven move and immediate Fed pricing.

For Broadcom, the next useful information is the final senior and junior sizing, guarantee scope, collateral and lease terms, ratings and funding sequence. The amount retained by banks and private-capital sponsors will help show where the risk ultimately sits. The headline maximum describes the ambition of the project; actual placement will establish its financing cost.
